Print method for stree objects

Source: R/print.R
print.stree.Rd

Prints the call, class levels, and a depth-first sketch of the fitted tree, showing at each internal node the one-vs-rest class used for the split (in the multi-class case) and its weighted impurity, and at each leaf the predicted class and number of training observations.

# S3 method for class 'stree'
print(x, show_probs = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model of class "stree".

show_probs

Logical; if TRUE, also print each leaf's class probability vector.

...

Currently unused; included for S3 method consistency.

Value

x, invisibly. Called for its side effect of printing to the console.

Examples

fit <- stree(Species ~ ., data = iris, max_depth = 3)
print(fit)
#> STree oblique classification tree
#> Call:  stree(formula = Species ~ ., data = iris, max_depth = 3)
#> Classes: setosa, versicolor, virginica 
#> Kernel: linear
#> 
#>  [Node] depth = 1 | n = 150 | kernel = linear | split: setosa vs rest | impurity = 0.6667
#>  |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#> |   [Leaf] predict = setosa | n = 50
#>  `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>     [Node] depth = 2 | n = 100 | kernel = linear
#>     |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#>    |   [Leaf] predict = versicolor | n = 46
#>     `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>        [Leaf] predict = virginica | n = 54
print(fit, show_probs = TRUE)
#> STree oblique classification tree
#> Call:  stree(formula = Species ~ ., data = iris, max_depth = 3)
#> Classes: setosa, versicolor, virginica 
#> Kernel: linear
#> 
#>  [Node] depth = 1 | n = 150 | kernel = linear | split: setosa vs rest | impurity = 0.6667
#>  |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#> |   [Leaf] predict = setosa | n = 50 | probs = [ 1, 0, 0 ]
#>  `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>     [Node] depth = 2 | n = 100 | kernel = linear
#>     |- Positive branch (distance > 0):
#>    |   [Leaf] predict = versicolor | n = 46 | probs = [ 0, 1, 0 ]
#>     `- Negative branch (distance <= 0):
#>        [Leaf] predict = virginica | n = 54 | probs = [ 0, 0.074, 0.926 ]
